Summary: Samuel judged Israel year by year on a circuit from his home at Ramah to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, then returned to Ramah, where his house was and where he built an altar. The text gives the circuit towns but not the order he visited them each year, so the stages list the towns rather than a fixed itinerary.
Significance: Samuel's circuit made justice and worship reachable: the judge came to the people instead of waiting for them to come to him.
